class.name: StairsBody
class.brief_description: Kinematic character body that walks up and down stairs inside its own move.
class.description: Kinematic character body with stair stepping built into its own move, rather than wrapped around [method CharacterBody3D.move_and_slide]. A frame pays for one set of sweeps instead of the slide's plus the step check's. Replaces [method CharacterBody3D.move_and_slide] entirely, so none of [CharacterBody3D]'s API exists here. The getters keep its names where no native method is in the way. Set [member velocity], optionally [member desired_velocity], then call [method move_and_stair_step] from [method Node._physics_process]. Physics queries per frame, the budget this class is built around: [codeblock lang=text] walking on flat ground 2 (the move sweep, the contact test) pressed into a wall 2 (the same two; the step attempt is cached) intent off the motion +1 (a sweep along intent, which only looks for a step) climbing a step 5 (move sweep, up, forward, down, contact test) leaving a floor +1 (the floor probe, only where contact is lost) on a moving platform +1 (the carry, as its own sweep) [/codeblock] Assumes world up is [constant Vector3.UP].

method.name: get_contact_collider
method.description: The object the contact at [param index] belongs to, or [code]null[/code] if it has been freed since the move. See [method get_contact_count] for which contacts are listed.

method.name: get_contact_collider_id
method.description: Instance id of the object the contact at [param index] belongs to. Cheaper than [method get_contact_collider] when only comparing ids.

method.name: get_contact_count
method.description: Number of contacts the last [method move_and_stair_step] made. Listed: each slide sweep's contact, the sweeps of a step the body committed, a moving floor's carry, the floor probe when it set the body down, and the resting contacts after the move, floor included. Not listed: the sweeps of a step that was refused. Cleared at the start of every move. A collider may appear more than once; the order carries no meaning.

method.name: get_contact_normal
method.description: Normal of the contact at [param index], pointing from the collider toward the body.

method.name: get_contact_position
method.description: Global position of the contact at [param index].

method.name: get_floor_normal
method.description: Normal of the floor found by the last move. Only meaningful while [method is_on_floor] is [code]true[/code].

method.name: get_platform_velocity
method.description: Velocity of the floor the body stands on, added to [member velocity] when the body leaves it.

method.name: get_wall_normal
method.description: Normal of the wall hit by the last move. Only meaningful while [method is_on_wall] is [code]true[/code].

method.name: is_on_ceiling
method.description: Whether the last move hit a ceiling.

method.name: is_on_floor
method.description: Whether the body ended the last move on a floor.

method.name: is_on_wall
method.description: Whether the last move hit a wall, or the body is being held still against one.

method.name: is_step_surface
method.description: Whether a step may be committed onto [param body]: anything the physics server is not simulating (static geometry, kinematic platforms, frozen rigid bodies) and not on [param ignore_layers]. A step is a teleport rather than a solve, so setting the body down on a simulating one leaves the solver to separate them by moving the only thing that can move, which raises the surface and offers the next frame a fresh step. Measured under Jolt: a loose 0.45 x 0.3 x 0.45 m crate lifted the body 1.085 m and left at 5.6 m/s, the same at 10 kg and 30 kg.

method.name: move_and_stair_step
method.description: Moves the body by [member velocity] for one physics frame, stepping up and down stairs. Call it from [method Node._physics_process].

members.member: Horizontal intent for this frame. Drives the step probe when velocity has been pinned near zero by the face it is pushing into. Cleared after each move.
Steepest surface that counts as floor, in radians.
Allow a step this frame even when airborne. Cleared after each move.
Slide iterations for the main move.
Smallest distance a step probe looks ahead, whatever the tick rate.
Collision margin used by every sweep.
How far the floor probe reaches down to stay on the ground or step down. Negative follows [member step_height].
Max height the body can step up onto.

Collision layers a step is never committed onto, though the body still collides with them: bodies too small or too self-driving to be a stair. Taken out of the body's mask while the step and floor-probe sweeps run, so those sweeps see the surface underneath instead. A floor on these layers holds the body up but never carries it as a platform: [method get_platform_velocity] stays zero on it.
Slide iterations for the forward leg of a step.
Velocity in m/s. Written back after each move: clipped against what the body hit, and with any downward part zeroed while on the floor.

signal.name: stepped
signal.description: Emitted on any stair step, in either direction, after the direction-specific one. [param delta] is the height the body moved, in metres: positive up, negative down.

signal.name: stepped_down
signal.description: Emitted when the floor probe has set the body down onto a lower surface. [param drop] is how far it went down, in metres, and is positive.

signal.name: stepped_up
signal.description: Emitted when the body has been raised onto a higher surface. [param rise] is how far it went up, in metres, and is positive.
